title: Medical Debt and Your Credit Report in 2026
description: The CFPB rule banning medical debt from credit reports was vacated in 2025. What protections remain, how to dispute errors and how to negotiate medical bills.
h1: Medical debt and your credit report: where things stand
intro: A federal rule that would have removed medical debt from credit reports never took effect: a federal court vacated it in July 2025. Here is what still protects you and what to do about a medical bill you cannot pay.

image.alt: Shopping cart filled with pills and money, illustrating healthcare costs

cardText: The CFPB rule banning medical debt from credit reports was vacated in 2025.

sections.h2: What happened to the federal rule
sections.html: In January 2025 the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) finalized a rule to stop most medical debt from appearing on credit reports. In July 2025 a federal court in Texas ruled the CFPB had exceeded its authority and vacated the rule.

• The three nationwide credit bureaus have voluntary policies that keep paid medical collections and smaller medical collection debts off reports, and wait before reporting new medical collections.
  • A number of states have their own laws limiting medical debt reporting.
  • You can dispute any inaccurate information with the credit bureau and the company that reported it.

1. Ask for an itemized bill and check it for errors.
  2. Check whether the No Surprises Act applies.
  3. Ask the hospital about financial assistance (charity care); nonprofit hospitals must have a policy.
  4. Negotiate a discount or an interest-free payment plan.
  5. Be cautious about putting medical bills on high-interest credit cards.

General information, not medical, legal or insurance advice. This post reflects the position on the date shown. Check the official sources below for the latest rules.

faqs.q: Is medical debt still on credit reports?
faqs.a: It can be. The CFPB rule was vacated, but bureau policies and some state laws keep many medical debts off reports.
